thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — elevated p99 latency observed on continuous-batching inference path in us-west-2. Auto-detected at 2025-10-12T03:12:51Z. Metrics: p95=210ms (norm ~45ms), p99=2.1s (norm ~180ms). Streaming stall count increased x7. Paging retries triggered for some batches. @violet oncall.

violet: on it. seeing the alert. paging now. any known deploys? :eyes:

raj: no deploys from infra. I can pull metrics and tail the runtime logs. pushing my dashboard link: https://dash.internal/redwood/contbatch/usw2

maya: customer-impact note: we have increased error rates for chunked streaming. Support ticket from PayC saying degraded assistant latency. Reached out to CS for details.

leo: adding context — overnight traffic shifted to a lot more short prompts and a small fraction of very long sequences. suspect mixed-seq length padding is amplifying batch sizes and causing KV cache thrash.

violet: good call. pax: can you confirm if KV evictions spiked? pulling evict metrics now.

alex: i see a big spike in kv_cache_evictions at 03:10Z, correlated with batch_size_avg jumping from 6 -> 18. That explains the p99 jump.

raj: logs (snippet):
```
2025-10-12T03:10:12Z runtime[worker-7]: batch assembled size=23 seqlen={12,14,512,8,6,4,1024,7,...}
2025-10-12T03:10:12Z runtime[worker-7]: kvcache miss ratio=0.77, evict_count=153
2025-10-12T03:10:13Z runtime[worker-7]: streaming stall detected: tail latency 2560ms
```

maya: customer impact: PayC calls are timing out at 10s on their side; CS escalated to SEs. We've flagged it as P2 for now because multiple customers hit higher latencies.

violet: live-mit steps: 1) throttle/burst limit incoming batching from inference-router for streaming routes 2) temporarily lower max_batch_size on `serve/streaming` to 12 3) enable parity scheduling fairness policy to prioritize short sequences 4) route heavy long seqs to fallback smaller-oz model (if compatible) 5) keep page open for handoff.

raj: executing step 2 and 3 now. command:
```
# set config on router
redwoodctl route update serve/streaming --max-batch-size=12 --scheduling=fair_short_first
```
response: accepted, change propagated to pool-usw2 in ~8s

# verify poller config
kubectl -n runtime get cm batcher-config -o yaml | grep max_batch_size
```

leo: saw immediate drop in average batch_size from 18 -> 10 within 40s. p95 down to ~120ms. p99 falling but still elevated at 600-800ms.

alex: streaming stalls reduced by ~60%. KV evictions trending down. good sign.

maya: I updated the CS ticket and notified the impacted customers; PayC acknowledged they're seeing improvement but want ETA for full resolution.

product-oncall: can we estimate risk of longer-term change? lowering max_batch_size will increase per-token cost. need an estimate of delta and whether to keep until root cause fixed.

violet: short-term keep limit for 30m while we investigate root cause. i'll start a pressure test to reproduce locally with mixed-seq workload and capture traces.

raj: running repro harness with seq distribution copied from traffic. early note: scheduler was favoring full-batches; fairness algorithm didn't preempt big sequences, so long seqs blocked small-keyed requests until KV warmups completed.

leo: hypothesis: mixed-seq arrival pattern + continuous-batching greedy fill -> padding amplification and huge cache churn. mitigation options: fair_short_first, seq-length bucketing, or dynamic per-request expected-kv hints from router.

alex: logs show one worker with repeated tail spikes due to swapping KV pages between model shards. we'll add a short-term patch to reduce KV eviction aggressiveness on hot workers.

violet: patch deploy plan: rollback not required — we will push hotfix to runtime config to increase kv_cache_size_pct for affected pool and enable per-worker kv_sticky flag. This should reduce evictions but may increase memory by ~8%.

raj: hotfix pushed to pool-usw2. command:
```
redwoodctl pool update pool-usw2 --kv-cache-pct=22 --kv-sticky=true
```
applied.

leo: monitoring: p99 back down to ~320ms within 2m. paging severity to be downgraded if stable for 10m.

maya: CS notified. PayC says performance acceptable now. keeping them updated.

product-oncall: flag for cost impact: expect small bump in infra memory usage and per-token cost due to smaller batches. we'll run Optimize to suggest quantization/other offsets.

violet: i'm handing off at 03:30Z to @raj who will own until 07:00Z. current state: mitigations active (max_batch_size=12, fair scheduling), p95 ~90-130ms, p99 ~300-450ms, KV evictions low. please escalate to eng-runtime if p99 creeps >800ms again.

raj: ack. i'll keep checks and follow up with post-incident notes. leaving open action items: 1) root cause deep-dive on scheduler policy with traces 2) consider seq-length bucketing 3) evaluate router-side kv hints 4) communicate cost tradeoffs to product/support.

alex: logging for postmortem saved to /var/log/contbatch/incidents/1761717171.log and exported to the incident archive.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — severity reduced to P3 at 2025-10-12T03:24:00Z. On-call handoff recorded: violet -> raj. Reminders: create postmortem if recurrence or customer SLA impact >1h.

violet: thanks team. i'll add initial notes to the incident doc and assign deep-dive owners. :thumbsup:

raj: starting a timeline and will ping eng-runtime and sched folks. leaving this thread open for updates.
